title: Uniformly bounded expected logarithmic prime-factor discrepancy in couplings of random integers and parameter-one Poisson–Dirichlet sequences
source_title: On Arratia’s coupling and the Dirichlet law for the factors of a random integer
author: Tony Haddad; Dimitris Koukoulopoulos
difficulty_reason: The published scale-invariant spacing, rearrangement and prime-number prerequisites alone yield neither a constant expected discrepancy nor the needed rare-event error. The authors change the extra-prime distribution to logarithmic weighting and control the rounding-induced cutoff and point-order changes by full dyadic and multivariate Mecke integral estimates at the sharper O(1/log x) scale. Their already-written uniform total-variation comparison then combines with the full rearrangement and rounding moment bounds to remove the remaining logarithmic loss.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Upper-bound part of Theorem1: for each x>=2, Nx is uniform on integers1..floor(x), its decreasing prime factors are padded with ones, and V has Poisson–Dirichlet law with parameter1. The authors construct a coupling with E sum_i |log(P_i)-V_i log(x)| bounded by an absolute constant. The exact abstract uses x>=2; the selected assertion is the upper bound, avoiding the printed lower-bound statement at x=1. Full explicit coupling10–12, rearrangement discrepancy13–14, GEM/Poisson and rounding moment15–16, integer-friendly process distribution16–18, new cutoff/order mismatch estimates18–23, and total variation closing23–24 read. Number-theoretic background/strong Mertens36–37 and exact maximal-coupling construction37–39 read. Named Arratia scale-invariant spacing lemma4.2/reference3 Lemma7.1, rearrangement reference3 Lemma3.2, prime number theoremreference13 Chapter8, and Campbell/Mecke tools39–40 are traced published background. No separate Dirichlet factorization outcome or conditional exponential-moment consequence is counted. Obvious duplicate search found only unrelated Arratia–Goldstein–Gordon Gaussian extreme-value coupling background, not this prime-factor/Poisson–Dirichlet claim. Whole41-page original context retained with original2025volume12 identity and pinned dates.

historical_source_pdf_evidence.original_difficulty_reason: The authors refine a scale-invariant Poisson coupling by logarithmically weighting an extra prime and control rare ordering and cutoff mismatches through multivariate Mecke estimates to obtain an optimal-order uniform discrepancy bound. This probabilistic analytic number theory exceeds ordinary qualifying examinations.
